correctness.rationale: Poisson marking splits pair-affecting resets into independent rates alpha,alpha,c; their union rate is delta. Conditioning on the last such reset gives exactly the integral of c Q_t(x)^2 plus 2alpha Q_t(x) E Q_t(x-Y) against exp(-delta t) dt, with Y Laplace rate k1=sqrt(lambda/D) and independent of subsequent Brownian noise. Mills ratios locate the unique saddle t*=x/sqrt(2Ddelta); Bessel K2 asymptotics give J(x)~exp(-k2 x)/(delta sqrt(2pi k2 x)). In the same saddle window Q_t(x-Y)/Q_t(x)->exp(k2Y/2); the Laplace moment equals 2lambda/c because k2/2<k1 for c>0. Strict exponential integrability plus saddle localization justify the tilt, yielding coefficient c+4alpha lambda/c. Independent integral quadrature at N,m=(5,2),(6,4),(3,2) confirmed positive ratios increasing toward 1 (convergence is especially slow when c small); it is not proof of an asymptotic. The c=0 boundary is exactly independent via Poisson thinning.
residual_risks: Fixed positive common-reset rate c and finite population are essential; expansion not uniform as c tends to zero.
Numerical finite-threshold ratios can be far from 1 when the tilted Laplace moment is near its integrability boundary; the asymptotic argument requires dominated saddle control.
